sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档聚焦设计之美及相关文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 回想当年我在黑胶唱片时代在夜店当DJ时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍爱的传家宝去工作，你把一个DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面陈列着美丽的长达50年的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 立即在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重塑者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Brussels Bureau Chief Matina Steves-Gridna.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是布鲁塞尔分社社长玛蒂娜·史蒂夫-格里德纳。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, New York Times Magazine writer Susan Dominus on menopause.
sentences.zh: 今天是《纽约时报杂志》撰稿人苏珊·多米努斯谈更年期。

sentences.en: She tells the story of how it's been misunderstood for years, both in society and by doctors, and what happened when her story about it went viral.
sentences.zh: 她讲述了多年来社会和医生对更年期存在多少误解，以及当她关于这个话题的文章走红时发生了什么。

sentences.en: It's Friday, July 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月28日，星期五。

sentences.en: Okay, we're recording now.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们现在开始录音了。

sentences.en: So I'm going to ask you a couple of questions, and one of them is just if you could describe to me some of the symptoms that you experienced.
sentences.zh: 所以我要问你几个问题，其中一个就是请你向我描述一下你所经历的一些症状。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So when I first started, am I going to say menopause journey?
sentences.zh: 那么当我刚开始时，我是要说更年期之旅吗？

sentences.en: I think I'm actually going to.
sentences.zh: 我想我其实会这么说。

sentences.en: When I first started the menopause journey.
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始经历更年期之旅时。

sentences.en: The first thing that I noticed were incredibly heavy periods.
sentences.zh: 我注意到的第一件事就是经量大得惊人。

sentences.en: Night sweats.
sentences.zh: 盗汗。

sentences.en: Consistent, recurring.
sentences.zh: 持续不断，反复出现。

sentences.en: Literally every two or three minutes.
sentences.zh: 字面意思上每两三分钟一次。

sentences.en: Uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 很不舒服。

sentences.en: Hot flushes.
sentences.zh: 潮热。

sentences.en: I'd wake up in the middle of the night with my hair, my pajamas, the pillow and sheets.
sentences.zh: 我会在半夜醒来，头发、睡衣、枕头和床单

sentences.en: Soaked.
sentences.zh: 全湿透了。

sentences.en: I would just lie in bed awake all night, sweating with my heart racing.
sentences.zh: 我会整夜醒着躺在床上，一边出汗一边心跳加速。

sentences.en: And I had small children, and you know, what I really noticed was that things that normally wouldn't bother me that they were doing would send me into orbit.
sentences.zh: 而且我有幼小的孩子，你知道，我真正注意到的是，他们做的一些平时不会困扰我的事情，会让我彻底抓狂。

sentences.en: I also did notice I would get actual migraines during my cycles.
sentences.zh: 我还注意到，在经期我会得真正的偏头痛。

sentences.en: I'd also get high anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我还会产生高度焦虑。

sentences.en: So that was really affecting me.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的对产生了很大影响。

sentences.en: My first sign was definitely hot flashes, but then there was something that I hadn't heard about, which is all of the moisture in my body left the building.
sentences.zh: 我的第一个迹象绝对是潮热，但接着出现了一件我从未听说过的事，那就是我体内的水分全跑光了。

sentences.en: Like, my eyes were dry, my scalp was dry, my nose was dry, my mouth was dry.
sentences.zh: 比如，我的眼睛干了，头皮干了，鼻子干了，嘴巴干了。

sentences.en: And then just keep on moving down the body and just know that every single place that was once moist was now dry.
sentences.zh: 然后顺着身体往下，你会发现曾经湿润的每一个地方现在都干涸了。

sentences.en: I was born in the 70s, and no one talked about menopause.
sentences.zh: 我出生在70年代，当时没有人谈论更年期。

sentences.en: It's not really spoken about.
sentences.zh: 这根本不怎么被讨论。

sentences.en: You know, I had told my doctors what I was experiencing, and they just didn't really say anything about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我曾把我的经历告诉过医生，但他们对此什么也没说。

sentences.en: The doctor I saw was a younger woman, probably in her 30s.
sentences.zh: 我见的那位医生是个年轻女性，大概30多岁。

sentences.en: She offered me supplements or anti-anxiety medication.
sentences.zh: 她给我推荐了保健品或者抗焦虑药物。

sentences.en: I think for myself, I thought I just kind of pushed through it.
sentences.zh: 我想对我自己来说，我以为我只是硬扛过去了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I would say it took me seven years before I got help.
sentences.zh: 对，我可以说我花了七年时间才得到帮助。

sentences.en: Treatment options, did I have any treatment options?
sentences.zh: 治疗选择，我有什么治疗选择吗？

sentences.en: I talked to my doctor, and I got the same whole kind of, there's cancer in your family, you're high risk.
sentences.zh: 我跟医生谈过，得到的还是那一套老话：你家族里有癌症病史，你是高危人群。

sentences.en: So there's nothing you can do except, you know, basically wear cardigans because they're the quickest sweater to take off.
sentences.zh: 所以你什么也做不了，除了——你知道的——基本上只能穿开衫，因为那是最好脱下来的毛衣。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: Susan, you wrote a story for the New York Times Magazine this year that became one of the most read stories of the year.
sentences.zh: 苏珊，今年你为《纽约时报杂志》写了一篇报道，成了今年阅读量最高的故事之一。

sentences.en: It got more than 3,000 comments on the article page, which is huge.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章在评论区获得了3000多条评论，这非常惊人。

sentences.en: And it ignited a really big, open conversation, which you yourself became a figure in.
sentences.zh: 它点燃了一场非常盛大、公开的对话，而你本人也成了其中的风云人物。

sentences.en: It was about menopause.
sentences.zh: 主题就是更年期。

sentences.en: Can you tell us why you wrote that story?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们你为什么要写这个故事吗？

sentences.en: I was interested in writing about menopause because even some of the smartest, most can-do women I knew,
sentences.zh: 我有兴趣写更年期，因为即使是我认识的最聪明、最能干的一些女性，

sentences.en: women who have tremendous agency and are great at research and are extremely efficient, were completely baffled by the subject.
sentences.zh: 那些拥有巨大自主权、擅长调研且极其高效的女性，也被这个主题彻底搞糊涂了。

sentences.en: They were confused about their symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 她们对自己的症状感到困惑。

sentences.en: They were confused about how menopause works.
sentences.zh: 她们对更年期是如何运作的感到困惑。

sentences.en: And they were absolutely searching for anything that would help them with the symptoms in ways that were very rarely successful.
sentences.zh: 她们绝对在寻找任何能帮助她们缓解症状的方法，但往往极少成功。

sentences.en: And then I myself started experiencing some of those symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 然后我自己也开始经历其中一些症状。

sentences.en: I was having hot flashes that woke me up in the middle of the night and often sent me into kind of an anxious spiral.
sentences.zh: 我开始出现潮热，半夜把我惊醒，并且经常让我陷入某种焦虑的漩涡。

sentences.en: I was having strange discomfort in my abdomen.
sentences.zh: 我的腹部有一种奇怪的不适感。

sentences.en: I felt sort of straight.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有点紧绷。

sentences.en: My body didn't feel familiar to me.
sentences.zh: 我的身体让我感到陌生。

sentences.en: And I was really having problems with my memory.
sentences.zh: 而且我的记忆力确实出现了问题。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: So I started having trouble recalling names, sometimes words.
sentences.zh: 我开始想不起名字，有时是词语。

sentences.en: It was, you know, it was bad enough that, like, my friends, or really my sister, was commenting on it.
sentences.zh: 这，你知道的，情况已经严重到我的朋友们，或者说我的姐姐，都开始对此指指点点了。

sentences.en: And I also thought it was a real thing.
sentences.zh: 我也觉得这是一件真实存在的事。

sentences.en: And I started thinking about a conversation I'd once had with a writer I really admire, someone who I knew had retired pretty young.
sentences.zh: 我开始想起我曾经和一个我非常钦佩的作家的一次谈话，我知道她很早就退休了。

sentences.en: When I saw her at a party at some point, I said to her, why did you stop writing?
sentences.zh: 有一次在派对上见到她时，我问她，你为什么不写了？

sentences.en: And she said, because of menopause.
sentences.zh: 她说，因为更年期。

sentences.en: The words just weren't coming.
sentences.zh: 词汇就是涌现不出来了。

sentences.en: And I honestly think I got, like, almost like a little chill at the time.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我当时甚至觉得，几乎可以说是有点不寒而栗。

sentences.en: And I've, you know, I've thought about it ever since.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，从那以后我一直在思考这件事。

sentences.en: So, what did you do?
sentences.zh: 所以，你做了什么？

sentences.en: So, it was time for me to see my OBGYN anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之，反正我也到了该去看妇产科医生的时候了。

sentences.en: And I thought, you know what?
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I'm going to bring these issues up with her.
sentences.zh: 我要和她谈谈这些问题。

sentences.en: They're enough of an issue in my life that I think it's, you know, worth talking about.
sentences.zh: 它们在我的生活中已经是个足够大的问题了，我觉得，你知道的，值得拿出来聊聊。

sentences.en: And I sort of described what I was going through, which was, I would say, on my mind, but they weren't dramatic.
sentences.zh: 我大致描述了我的经历，我想这些都在我脑海里，但并不算戏剧化。

sentences.en: I wasn't having 17 hot flashes a day.
sentences.zh: 我没有一天经历17次潮热。

sentences.en: Some women do.
sentences.zh: 有些女性确实会有。

sentences.en: But when I mentioned them to her, I remember she said, we only treat significant symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 但当我向她提及这些时，我记得她说，我们只治疗明显的症状。

sentences.en: And I definitely felt a little ashamed that I had, you know, dared to complain about these issues.
sentences.zh: 我确实感到有点羞耻，因为我竟然，你知道的，敢于抱怨这些问题。

sentences.en: And I just was wondering to myself, like, well, all right, were they significant?
sentences.zh: 我当时就在想，好吧，这些算明显吗？

sentences.en: What does significant mean exactly?
sentences.zh: 明显到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: I mean, they were significant enough to me that I brought them up, you know, that they were on my mind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对它们对我来说足够明显，所以我才提出来，它们一直在我的脑海里。

sentences.en: And how did this doctor's appointment end?
sentences.zh: 那这次看医生是怎么结束的？

sentences.en: Like, did you end up asking for treatment?
sentences.zh: 比如，你最后要求治疗了吗？

sentences.en: Did you push back on this concept of significant symptoms?
sentences.zh: 你对“明显症状”这个概念提出异议了吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: You know, in her defense, you know, doctors have such short windows.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，为她辩护一下，医生们的看诊时间实在太短了。

sentences.en: She had things to do, pap smears to take.
sentences.zh: 她有很多事要做，还要做宫颈涂片检查。

sentences.en: Like, I just, you know, felt a little bad and left, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我只是觉得有点不好意思，然后就离开了。

sentences.en: So after that, I really wanted to start to get a handle on the material, or at least to try to.
sentences.zh: 所以在那之后，我真的很想开始掌控这些资料，或者至少尝试去掌控。

sentences.en: I was confused.
sentences.zh: 我很困惑。

sentences.en: My friends were confused.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友们也很困惑。

sentences.en: And I really wanted answers.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想要答案。

sentences.en: And when I started researching the topic, I realized pretty quickly that the history of menopause in this country
sentences.zh: 当我开始研究这个课题时，我很快意识到，这个国家更年期的历史

sentences.en: is sort of a history of misinformation or lack of information, lack of research.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上就是一部充满虚假信息、或者说缺乏信息与研究的历史。

sentences.en: It's a topic that has just been so shrouded in ignorance, really, that it took a lot of work to unearth
sentences.zh: 这是一个被无知重重包裹的话题，以至于需要付出大量的工作，才能发掘出

sentences.en: facts that are well-known to the medical community, but somehow haven't really translated into information for everyday women.
sentences.zh: 医学界早已熟知、但不知为何并未真正转化为普通女性所了解的信息的事实。

sentences.en: Okay, so what is the history of menopause, and how did you arrive at that conclusion?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么更年期的历史到底是怎样的，你是如何得出这个结论的？

sentences.en: So far as I know, women have been reaching menopause since time immemorial.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，自古以来女性就一直在经历更年期。

sentences.en: But we basically say that a woman is menopausal when a year has gone by and she has not had her period for that period of time.
sentences.zh: 但我们基本上把一个女性定义为进入更年期，当她已经有一整年没有来过月经。

sentences.en: And perimenopause is the time leading up to that, which is a time of a lot of kind of intense hormonal fluctuations.
sentences.zh: 而围绝经期是之前的时期，这是一个伴随着大量剧烈荷尔蒙波动的时期。

sentences.en: It can last anywhere from four months to a decade.
sentences.zh: 它可以持续四个月到十年不等。

sentences.en: And interestingly, there's research that suggests that for Latina women and Black women, it can last even longer and start earlier.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，有研究表明，对于拉丁裔女性和黑人女性来说，这个时期可能会持续更久，而且开始得更早。

sentences.en: But for a very long time, it was just something that women had to deal with.
sentences.zh: 但在很长一段时间里，这只是女性不得不默默忍受的事情。

sentences.en: And menopause was not exactly part of the mainstream conversation until 1966, when a British gynecologist named Robert Wilson published a book called Feminine Forever.
sentences.zh: 直到1966年，一位名叫罗伯特·威尔逊的英国妇科医生出版了一本名为《永远的女性》的书，更年期才真正成为主流对话的一部分。

sentences.en: And it shifted the conversation around menopause and what could be done about it and suggested that hormone treatment,
sentences.zh: 这本书改变了人们对更年期及应对方法的看法，并提出荷尔蒙疗法——

sentences.en: which had been around for a few years but wasn't widely used, could keep women young and beautiful and sexual.
sentences.zh: 这种疗法已经存在几年但未被广泛使用——可以让女性保持年轻、美丽和性感。

sentences.en: And the book was also sort of empowering in that way.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，这本书在某种程度上也是一种赋权。

sentences.en: But it was also a little bit promising that maybe they'd be easier on their husbands and they'd also be more desirable.
sentences.zh: 但它同时也带有一种承诺，也许她们对丈夫会更有耐心，同时也会更有吸引力。

sentences.en: And there was this idea, you know, take estrogen because it'll make your husband's life better too.
sentences.zh: 当时有这样一种观点，你知道的，使用雌激素吧，因为这也会让丈夫的生活更美好。

sentences.en: So, for example, he writes, quote, all postmenopausal women are castrates, end quote.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，他写道：“所有绝经后的女性都是被阉割的人。”

sentences.en: But he said that if a woman were to use estrogen, quote,
sentences.zh: 但他说，如果女性使用雌激素，

sentences.en: her breasts and genital organs will not shrivel, she will be much more pleasant to live with and will not become dull and unattractive, end quote.
sentences.zh: “她们的乳房和生殖器官不会萎缩，与她们生活在一起会愉快得多，也不会变得沉闷和毫无吸引力。”

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it's like, here's this thing that will help alleviate women's suffering.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好像是，这里有一个能减轻女性痛苦的东西。

sentences.en: But basically, we're just going to package it with men in mind.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，我们把它和男性的需求捆绑在了一起。

sentences.en: I think he was doing something complicated, which is he was genuinely helping women feel empowered about their sex lives.
sentences.zh: 我认为他在做一件复杂的事情，那就是他真诚地帮助女性在性生活上感到更有自主权。

sentences.en: But it was, I think, at a moment in time when you couldn't just empower women, you also needed to reassure their husbands maybe that there was something in it for them as well.
sentences.zh: 但我想，在那样的时代背景下，你不仅要赋予女性权力，也许你还需要向她们的丈夫保证，他们也能从中得到好处。

sentences.en: But women seem convinced and they start taking it in droves, frankly.
sentences.zh: 但女性似乎被说服了，坦白说，她们开始蜂拥使用。

sentences.en: There was a brief blip in the mid-70s when doctors realized that taking estrogen alone increased the risk of endometrial cancer.
sentences.zh: 在70年代中期曾有过短暂的波折，当时医生们意识到单用雌激素会增加子宫内膜癌的风险。

sentences.en: So then they started adding in progesterone, which helped address that concern.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始加入孕激素，这有助于解决这一担忧。

sentences.en: And after that, I would say hormone use resumed full force.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，可以说荷尔蒙的使用全面恢复了。

sentences.en: You know, over the years, it became, you know, part of popular culture.
sentences.zh: 你知道，多年来，它成为了流行文化的一部分。

sentences.en: There's a famous episode of the classic TV show from the 1970s, All in the Family, in which poor Edith, the mother of the family, is really suffering from menopausal symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 1970年代经典电视剧《全家福》中有一个著名的插曲，剧中可怜的伊迪，也就是家里的母亲，正饱受更年期症状的折磨。

sentences.en: Hey, hey, there you are.
sentences.zh: 嘿，嘿，你在这儿呢。

sentences.en: Gee, we're waiting here.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我们都在这儿等着呢。

sentences.en: We're stopped.
sentences.zh: 我们都停下来了。

sentences.en: Don't rush me, Archie Bunker.
sentences.zh: 别催我，阿奇·邦克。

sentences.en: You get your dinner on time.
sentences.zh: 你的晚餐准时送上。

sentences.en: You always get your dinner on time.
sentences.zh: 你的晚餐总是准时送上的。

sentences.en: And they show her being unusually irritable and angry with everyone.
sentences.zh: 镜头展现出她异常暴躁，对每个人都充满了愤怒。

sentences.en: What's the matter with mom?
sentences.zh: 妈妈怎么了？

sentences.en: I was going to ask you.
sentences.zh: 我还想问你呢。

sentences.en: You know, she is going through these mood swings.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她正在经历这些情绪波动。

sentences.en: You ain't mad at nothing?
sentences.zh: 你难道不是对什么都不满吗？

sentences.en: Mad?
sentences.zh: 不满？

sentences.en: What would I be mad about?
sentences.zh: 我有什么好不满的？

sentences.en: Here's your beer.
sentences.zh: 给你你的啤酒。

sentences.en: You know, she starts taking these little pills to help her that the doctor prescribes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她开始吃医生开的这些小药丸来帮助自己。

sentences.en: Ah, it should be all right.
sentences.zh: 啊，这应该没问题。

sentences.en: These are these hormones, which, by the way, the hormones are pretty hot stuff, you know.
sentences.zh: 这些就是荷尔蒙，顺便说一句，荷尔蒙可是相当厉害的东西，你知道的。

sentences.en: And so the culture really was reflecting the reality of just how commonly prescribed hormones were at that time.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的文化确实反映了当时荷尔蒙处方有多么普遍的现实。

sentences.en: I've taken control of my life, and I keep up on things that affect my health, like estrogen loss at menopause.
sentences.zh: 我已经掌控了自己的生活，并且持续关注那些影响我健康的事物，比如更年期带来的雌激素流失。

sentences.en: Lauren Hutton, who was at the time a very admired former model turned actress, was featured on a commercial for hormone therapy.
sentences.zh: 劳伦·赫顿，当时是一位备受尊崇的前模特兼演员，她出现在了一则荷尔蒙疗法的商业广告中。

sentences.en: Ask your doctor what you can do to protect your health during and after menopause.
sentences.zh: 咨询你的医生，看看在更年期期间及之后，你能做些什么来保护你的健康。

sentences.en: Believe me, the time to protect your future is now.
sentences.zh: 相信我，保护你未来的时机就是现在。

sentences.en: You know, one doctor said that people believed it was so great for women's health that this one doctor told me she had it in one of the slides she would present,
sentences.zh: 你知道，曾有一位医生说，人们曾经认为它对女性健康太好了，以至于一位医生告诉我，她在展示的幻灯片里提到过，

sentences.en: saying that estrogen should be in the water.
sentences.zh: 说雌激素应该加到自来水里。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, as menopausal treatment is becoming incredibly popular,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，正当更年期治疗变得极其受欢迎的时候，

sentences.en: there was a faction of activists who were really concerned that we really didn't know what the health benefits were or the risks,
sentences.zh: 有一派活动人士真正担心的是，我们实际上并不清楚它的健康益处或风险到底是什么

sentences.en: because there had never been a large randomized control trial to study that.
sentences.zh: 因为此前从来没有过大型的随机对照试验来研究这一点。

sentences.en: And so in the mid-90s, the National Institutes of Health, led by Bernadine Healy, the first female leader of the NIH, started this massive,
sentences.zh: 所以在90年代中期，在NIH首位女性负责人伯纳丁·希利（Bernadine Healy）的领导下，美国国立卫生研究院启动了一项庞大的、

sentences.en: massive randomized control trial that would include research on the health benefits and risks of estrogen and progestogen.
sentences.zh: 一项涵盖雌激素和孕激素对健康益处及风险研究的庞大随机对照试验。

sentences.en: So this is a significant investment in researching this basically critical stage in every woman's life that so far just hadn't really been understood all that well.
sentences.zh: 因此，这项研究对几乎每个女性人生中这个至关重要、而此前却一直没有得到充分理解的阶段投入了巨资。

sentences.en: Yes, there's no doubt that this was a really important moment in women's health history, I would say.
sentences.zh: 是的，毫无疑问，这是女性健康史上一个非常重要的时刻。

sentences.en: So they recruit these thousands of women, they randomize the users of the hormone, they have control group, it's going along.
sentences.zh: 于是他们招募了数千名女性，随机分配激素使用者，设立对照组，研究顺利进行着。

sentences.en: And then in 2002, the people in charge of the trial call this huge press conference.
sentences.zh: 接着在2002年，试验负责人召开了这场大型新闻发布会。

sentences.en: For the millions of women taking or considering the combination hormone therapy estrogen and progestin, finally, some conclusive answers.
sentences.zh: 对于数百万正在服用或考虑联合使用雌激素和孕激素疗法的女性来说，终于有了确凿的答案。

sentences.en: And they announced that they are abruptly stopping the trial because they had found, they had reached a certain threshold of risk for women who are using the hormones.
sentences.zh: 他们宣布突然叫停这项试验，因为他们发现，使用激素的女性的风险已经达到了某个阈值。

sentences.en: Such that they had no choice, but ethically to stop the trial.
sentences.zh: 以至于从伦理上讲，他们别无选择，只能叫停试验。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: The government is shutting down a major study of hormone replacement therapy in women because of serious health concerns.
sentences.zh: 由于严重的健康隐患，政府正在叫停一项关于女性激素替代疗法的大型研究。

sentences.en: The combination of estrogen with progestin does not improve long-term health because there's increased risk of breast cancer, of heart attacks, stroke, blood clots.
sentences.zh: 雌激素与孕激素的联合使用并不能改善长期健康，因为这会增加患乳腺癌、心脏病、中风和血栓的风险。

sentences.en: They found increased rates of heart disease, of clotting, of stroke, and of breast cancer.
sentences.zh: 他们发现心脏病、血栓、中风和乳腺癌的发病率有所上升。

sentences.en: In the study, compared to women taking placebo, those on estrogen and progestin together had a 22% higher risk of heart disease, 26% higher risk of breast cancer,
sentences.zh: 在这项研究中，与服用安慰剂的女性相比，同时使用雌激素和孕激素的女性患心脏病的风险高出22%，患乳腺癌的风险高出26%，

sentences.en: and a 41% higher risk of stroke.
sentences.zh: 患中风的风险高出41%。

sentences.en: And as you can imagine, this was very, very big news.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的，这是一个非常非常大的新闻。

sentences.en: Tonight, the wonder has come out of hormone replacement therapy.
sentences.zh: 今晚，激素替代疗法走下了神坛。

sentences.en: I think the majority of women taking this combination therapy will be told by their physicians to stop.
sentences.zh: 我想，大多数服用这种联合疗法的女性都会被医生告知停药。

sentences.en: There's just this sense of dire concern that these risks were elevated, and women responded in droves to this fear.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种大难临头的担忧，认为这些风险加剧了，女性们纷纷对这种恐惧做出反应。

sentences.en: And they were calling their doctors, they were throwing their hormones, you know, flushing them down the toilet.
sentences.zh: 她们给医生打电话，把激素扔掉，你知道的，冲进马桶里。

sentences.en: So it sets off basically a panic.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上引发了一场恐慌。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: One doctor I interviewed said that she remembered when JFK was shot, she remembered 9-11,
sentences.zh: 我采访过的一位医生说，她记得肯尼迪总统遭枪击的时候，她记得9·11事件，

sentences.en: and she remembered the day of the WHI press conference because she had never received that many calls in one day.
sentences.zh: 她还记得WHI新闻发布会的那天，因为她从未在一天之内接到过那么多电话。

sentences.en: So clearly this is a huge shift for women.
sentences.zh: 显然，这对女性来说是一个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: And I have to imagine it comes with some anger that women were sort of given this treatment that was supposed to help them.
sentences.zh: 我能想象这伴随着一种愤怒，因为女性被给予了这种本该帮助她们的治疗。

sentences.en: But now they're thinking it's actually putting them in danger of grave disease like cancer.
sentences.zh: 但现在她们认为这实际上让她们陷入了癌症等严重疾病的危险之中。

sentences.en: Yes, I think that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想完全是这样。

sentences.en: And I also think a lot of doctors felt a lot of guilt that they had been prescribing this so aggressively to women of all ages under the assumption that it was going to be this kind of miracle cure.
sentences.zh: 而且我也认为很多医生感到非常内疚，因为他们曾假设这是一种奇迹般的疗法，从而向所有年龄段的女性如此激进地开出这种药。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so because of this press conference and the huge impact that it had, women really stopped asking their doctors about it.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于这次新闻发布会及其产生的巨大影响，女性真的不再向医生咨询这件事了。

sentences.en: Doctors, not all, but many, kind of stopped prescribing it or recommending it and started discouraging women from using menopausal hormone therapy.
sentences.zh: 医生们——并非全部，但很多——停止开药或推荐这种疗法，并开始阻止女性使用绝经期激素疗法。

sentences.en: And medical schools pretty much stopped teaching it.
sentences.zh: 医学院也几乎不再教授这门课程。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And menopausal hormone therapy basically just fell off the map.
sentences.zh: 而绝经期激素疗法基本上从人们的视野中消失了。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题是这样的。

sentences.en: There's a way of looking at all that information that is much more nuanced and allows much more for women's agency.
sentences.zh: 有一种方法可以更细致地看待所有这些信息，并且能更多地赋予女性自主权。

sentences.en: And because of the way the information was delivered and the way it was interpreted by the medical community,
sentences.zh: 由于信息的传达方式以及医学界的解读方式，

sentences.en: millions of women probably have suffered needlessly over the decades since.
sentences.zh: 在之后的几十年里，数百万女性可能一直在遭受不必要的痛苦。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.zh: 探索太空七十年。

sentences.zh: 我们想要探索下一颗星星之外的世界。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来陪伴您理解世界，充实每一天。

sentences.zh: 立即访问NYTimes.com/subscribe订阅，享受特惠。

sentences.en: So, Susan, you said that the findings from that big study and the risks of hormone therapy, that the way they were presented led to a misinterpretation.
sentences.zh: 那么，苏珊，你提到那项大型研究的结果以及激素疗法的风险，其呈现方式导致了误解。

sentences.en: How exactly was the study misinterpreted?
sentences.zh: 这项研究究竟是如何被误解的？

sentences.en: So, there were several ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几种方式。

sentences.en: One thing we do know is that the public has a pretty poor understanding of how to think about risk statistics.
sentences.zh: 我们知道的一点是，公众对如何看待风险统计数据的理解相当薄弱。

sentences.en: So, you know, if a woman's risk of having breast cancer between the ages of 50 and 60 is around 2.33%.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，如果一个50到60岁之间的女性患乳腺癌的风险大约是2.33%。

sentences.en: If you increase that risk by 26%, which is what the study did find for the women who were on those hormones, then you get something like 2.94%.
sentences.zh: 如果你把这个风险增加26%，这正是该研究对使用这些激素的女性所发现的数据，那么你得到的结果大约是2.94%。

sentences.en: And that is an increase, but it might be small enough of an increase that for some women it would be a risk they'd be willing to take.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个增长，但对于某些女性来说，这个增幅可能小到可以作为她们愿意承担的风险。

sentences.en: And it's a risk level that only kicks in after five years of use or so, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这个风险水平大约在使用五年后才会显现出来。

sentences.en: So, I think there was not a lot of context.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为当时缺乏很多背景信息。

sentences.en: And when people hear something like a 26% increased risk, maybe they think, oh, that means I have a 26% chance now of getting this cancer.
sentences.zh: 当人们听到诸如风险增加26%这样的话时，也许他们会想，哦，这意味着我现在有26%的几率患上这种癌症。

sentences.en: Or they don't know what the starting point is.
sentences.zh: 或者他们根本不知道起点是什么。

sentences.en: So, it's hard to interpret it without really getting into the nitty-gritty, but those things are really important.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果不深入探讨细节很难解读它，但这些细节真的很重要。

sentences.en: And there were a lot of good things that came out that were overlooked in the aftermath of this huge news story about how dangerous they were.
sentences.zh: 在这场关于它们有多危险的巨大新闻报道之后，其实产生了很多被忽视的好结果。

sentences.en: So, there was research that suggests that for women who start hormones in their 50s, you know, before the age of 60 or within 10 years of going through menopause,
sentences.zh: 例如，有研究表明，对于在50多岁（60岁之前，或绝经后10年内）开始使用激素的女性，

sentences.en: that there actually could be cardiovascular benefits if they started taking the hormone earlier rather than later.
sentences.zh: 如果她们提早而不是推迟开始使用激素，实际上可能会带来心血管益处。

sentences.en: And there was another arm of the trial that only studied women who had had hysterectomies who did not need to take progestogen.
sentences.zh: 还有试验的另一分支，仅研究了切除子宫且无需使用孕激素的女性。

sentences.en: And those women actually had a decreased risk of breast cancer and overall better long-term health outcomes,
sentences.zh: 这些女性患乳腺癌的风险实际上有所降低，整体长期健康状况也更好，

sentences.en: which is meaningful because something like a third of women by the age of 50 have had hysterectomies.
sentences.zh: 这很有意义，因为大约有三分之一的女性在50岁时切除了子宫。

sentences.en: Other research came out that found that using hormones could lower the risk of diabetes, and we certainly knew it lowered the risk of osteoporosis,
sentences.zh: 其他研究发现，使用激素可以降低患糖尿病的风险，我们当然也知道它能降低患骨质疏松症的风险，

sentences.en: which for many women is really important in terms of quality of life, in terms of mobility.
sentences.zh: 这对于许多女性在生活质量和行动能力方面至关重要。

sentences.en: But it wasn't the job of the people conducting these trials to evaluate quality of life issues.
sentences.zh: 但评估生活质量问题并不是进行这些试验的人的工作。

sentences.en: That's not what they intended to do, and it really wouldn't have been appropriate.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们的初衷，而且也确实不太合适。

sentences.en: But because that countervailing issue wasn't ever presented, I think it got lost in this larger dialogue.
sentences.zh: 但由于这种对立的问题从未被提出，我认为它在更大的对话中迷失了。

sentences.en: So actually, a better version of the coverage could have been something like hormone therapy could mean increased risk of breast cancer and other things like stroke or blood clots.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，更好的报道版本应该是这样的：激素疗法可能意味着会增加患乳腺癌以及中风或血栓等其他问题的风险。

sentences.en: But that risk is still limited and, most importantly, should be weighed against the benefits that we know that women experience through this treatment.
sentences.zh: 但这种风险仍然是有限的，最重要的是，应该将其与我们所知的女性通过这种治疗获得的益处进行权衡。

sentences.en: But instead, it was conveyed as representing this huge risk.
sentences.zh: 然而，它却被传达为代表着一种巨大的风险。

sentences.en: And so, no wonder everyone basically stopped taking it.
sentences.zh: 因此，难怪每个人基本上都停止服用了。

sentences.en: I think that's really accurate.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的很准确。

sentences.en: It was understood to be a really dramatic, really scary risk.
sentences.zh: 它被理解为一种非常戏剧化、非常可怕的风险。

sentences.en: And, you know, epidemiologically across a population, it's not nothing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，从整个人群的流行病学角度来看，这并非毫无影响。

sentences.en: It is a thing.
sentences.zh: 它确实是一回事。

sentences.en: But just there was no context and there was no opportunity for women to have the agency to think in an informed way about what that risk was.
sentences.zh: 只是当时缺乏背景，也没有给女性提供自主权，让她们以知情的方式去思考这种风险到底是什么。

sentences.en: So when you begin to engage in this question for yourself and you look at what your options are,
sentences.zh: 所以，当你开始为自己思考这个问题并查看有哪些选择时，

sentences.en: you're basically walking into a world that's sort of still dealing with the aftermath of this misinterpretation and misunderstanding.
sentences.zh: 你基本上是走进了一个仍在处理这种误解和错判余波的世界。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was walking into a world in which, although there were always doctors who did prescribe menopausal hormone therapy,
sentences.zh: 是的，我走进了一个这样的世界：尽管总有一些医生会开具绝经期激素疗法，

sentences.en: it was really not well understood by doctors who were coming up.
sentences.zh: 但新一代的医生对它其实并不十分了解。

sentences.en: There were plenty of doctors who just were like, yeah, you've reached menopause, nothing we can do about it.
sentences.zh: 有很多医生态度就是：没错，你绝经了，我们对此束手无策。

sentences.en: I do think that there was a lot of a sort of casual suck it up tone, you know, that took over.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为当时充斥着一种随意的“忍着点”的论调，你知道的。

sentences.en: And to me, it sort of merges with the general misogynistic ageist reality that older women are the last group it's agreed can be the target of insensitive jokes.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这与普遍存在的厌女和年龄歧视现实融为一体，即老年女性被默认是可以成为麻木不仁笑话靶子的最后一个人群。

sentences.en: Jokes about their undesirability, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，关于她们失去吸引力的笑话。

sentences.en: It's just this feeling that older women are not treated with respect and care.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉就是，老年女性没有得到尊重和关爱。

sentences.zh: 你觉得呢，布兰奇？

sentences.en: Am I through with my cycle?
sentences.zh: 我的月经周期结束了吗？

sentences.en: Well, I'd say menopause is a pretty good guess.

sentences.zh: 这次生育创造了摩擦力的纪录。

sentences.en: You and I, I have to be honest, that Jake Silverstein came to me, my editor at the New York Times Magazine, the editor-in-chief, wanting me to write a big story about menopause.
sentences.zh: 说实话，杰克·西尔弗斯坦（Jake Silverstein）——《纽约时报杂志》的主编、总编辑——找到我，希望我写一篇关于更年期的长篇大论。

sentences.en: And it's fascinating to me now that I actually hesitated.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，我居然犹豫了，这让我觉得很神奇。

sentences.en: I actually wasn't sure that it was a topic that I wanted to be too closely associated with.
sentences.zh: 我当时其实并不确定这是一个我想与之联系太紧密的话题。

sentences.en: You know, my college friends, when I told them that, they said, but that's why you have to write the article is because it needs to be destigmatized.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我把这告诉大学朋友时，她们说，但这就是你必须写这篇文章的原因，因为它需要去除污名化。

sentences.en: And, of course, they were 100% right.
sentences.zh: 当然，她们百分之百是对的。

sentences.en: And I'm glad that I did because not only was it a pretty fascinating inquiry, to me at least,
sentences.zh: 我很庆幸我写了，因为这不仅是一次相当迷人的探索，至少对我而言是这样，

sentences.en: but it also brought me up to speed on the range of options that are now available to women who are seeking relief for menopausal suffering.
sentences.zh: 它还让我了解了目前可供寻求缓解更年期痛苦的女性使用的一系列选择。

sentences.en: Like what kind of options?
sentences.zh: 比如有哪些选择？

sentences.en: So there's really been a lot of development of other kinds of ways of administering hormones for women who need care.
sentences.zh: 所以，针对需要护理的女性，目前在施用激素的其他方式上确实有了很多发展。

sentences.en: There are patches that are lower doses.
sentences.zh: 有剂量较低的贴片。

sentences.en: There's a micronized progesterone that it's hoped that that's closer to women's own progesterone, such that perhaps the risk of breast cancer might be lowered.
sentences.zh: 还有一种微粒化孕酮，人们希望它更接近女性自身的孕酮，从而可能会降低患乳腺癌的风险。

sentences.en: And for women with a cancer history who are not strong candidates for menopausal hormone therapy, now there's a drug on the market.
sentences.zh: 对于有癌症病史、不适合采用绝经期激素疗法的女性，市面上现在有一种药。

sentences.en: Hopefully, insurance will eventually cover it called Vioza, that is a non-hormonal option for treating hot flashes.
sentences.zh: 希望保险最终能报销这种名为Vioza的药，它是治疗潮热的一种非激素选择。

sentences.en: And there are new ways of getting good care from doctors trained in menopausal health by telemedicine.
sentences.zh: 还有通过远程医疗从受过更年期健康培训的医生那里获得优质护理的新途径。

sentences.en: There are online subscription services that make it extremely easy to get access to the hormones.
sentences.zh: 有一些在线订阅服务，让获取激素变得极其容易。

sentences.en: And obviously, these things take time.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这些事情都需要时间。

sentences.en: I think it's going to be a big learning curve, both for doctors and how to make this information available in a way that is both concise but nuanced,
sentences.zh: 我认为这将是一个巨大的学习曲线，无论是对医生而言，如何以简明而又细致的方式提供这些信息，

sentences.en: and for patients to learn that this is something that they have the right at least to consider.
sentences.zh: 还是对患者而言，了解到这是她们至少有权考虑的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But also in the culture, especially in the past few years,
sentences.zh: 但同样在文化中，特别是在过去几年里，

sentences.en: there's been a new conversation about menopause itself.
sentences.zh: 出现了一种关于更年期本身的新对话。

sentences.en: We're talking about what my friend Maria Schreiber and I call the big M.
sentences.zh: 我们在谈论我的朋友玛丽亚·施赖伯（Maria Schreiber）和我所称的“大M”（更年期）。

sentences.en: You know, Oprah has talked about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，奥普拉谈论过它。

sentences.en: I, too, am a hormone taker.
sentences.zh: 我也是一名激素服用者。

sentences.en: Michelle Obama has talked openly about it.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔·奥巴马也曾公开谈论过它。

sentences.en: Just hot flashes.
sentences.zh: 只是潮热。

sentences.en: I mean, I had a few before I started taking hormones.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在我开始服用激素之前我有过几次。

sentences.en: I remember having one on Marine One.
sentences.zh: 我记得在海军陆战队一号上时有过一次。

sentences.en: So I do think there's really positive change in all of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为这一切都在发生着非常积极的变化。

sentences.en: You cannot outrun, you cannot out-earn, you cannot out-exercise, you cannot out-yoga, you cannot out-fox the big M.
sentences.zh: 你无法跑赢、无法赚过、无法通过锻炼胜过、无法通过瑜伽摆脱、无法智胜“大M”。

sentences.en: You cannot.
sentences.zh: 你绝对无法逃脱。

sentences.en: The menopause train is coming no matter what.
sentences.zh: 更年期的列车无论如何都会开来。

sentences.en: So by the time my article was published...
sentences.zh: 所以到我的文章发表时……

sentences.en: This article just came out in the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章刚刚在《纽约时报》上发表。

sentences.en: I think what I wrote really kind of hit a nerve.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我写的内容确实触动了某些敏感神经。

sentences.en: Women have been misled about menopause.
sentences.zh: 女性在更年期方面一直被误导。

sentences.en: But that was a nerve that was already a little bit live before I got there.
sentences.zh: 但那原本就是一个在我介入之前就已经有点紧绷的神经。

sentences.en: Susan, let's start with you because I've even had friends who've asked me about it as recently as...
sentences.zh: 苏珊，我们从你开始，因为我甚至有朋友最近向我打听...

sentences.en: Unless you live under a rock, you most likely have seen it or been sent it by a friend...
sentences.zh: 除非你与世隔绝，否则你很可能已经看过它，或者是由朋友转发给你的...

sentences.en: It seemed to really connect with women who wanted a lot of information in one place.
sentences.zh: 它似乎真正连接了那些希望在一个地方获取大量信息的女性。

sentences.en: It is one of the best things as a woman in menopause I have ever read.
sentences.zh: 作为一名处于更年期的女性，这是我读过的最好的东西之一。

sentences.en: You are going to see yourself in the stories...
sentences.zh: 你会在这些故事中看到自己的影子...

sentences.en: And a lot of, I think, frankly, voicing of what they had been going through.
sentences.zh: 而且坦率地说，我认为其中很大程度上表达了她们一直以来的经历。

sentences.en: I just think it was a quick way to convey to people around them that menopause is no joke.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这是一种快捷的方式，向周围的人传达更年期绝非开玩笑。

sentences.en: You know, that it is a real thing in women's lives and it needs to be taken seriously.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是女性生活中真实存在的事情，必须认真对待。

sentences.en: And it's shocking, frankly, that it hasn't been talked about from the rooftops for longer than it has.
sentences.zh: 而且坦率地说，令人震惊的是，这么久以来竟然没有人大大方方地公开谈论它。

sentences.en: So your article clearly struck this nerve.
sentences.zh: 所以你的文章显然触及了这个痛点。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering if you know whether things have actually shifted inside the doctor's office for women who are literally going through this right now.
sentences.zh: 但我想知道，对于那些目前正经历这一切的女性来说，你是否知道诊所里的情况是否真的发生了变化。

sentences.en: So I do think for women who are going through this now, I'd like to think that the door has been opened for more of those conversations by the work that's been collectively done.
sentences.zh: 所以我的确认为，对于现在正经历这一切的女性来说，我愿意相信，通过大家共同努力的成果，为更多这样的对话打开了大门。

sentences.en: I mean, just, you know, some doctors have told me that they have a QR code that they give to women so that they can read the article.
sentences.zh: 我是说，就是，你知道，有些医生告诉我，他们有一个二维码可以发给女性，这样她们就可以阅读这篇文章。

sentences.en: Doctors have told me they now have waiting lists because so many people are coming in to talk about something that they didn't realize was even a topic of conversation they should be engaging in.
sentences.zh: 医生告诉我，他们现在有了候诊名单，因为有太多人前来谈论一些她们甚至不知道自己应该参与讨论的话题。

sentences.en: And I don't know, I personally found it very moving that my friend's daughter, a college student,
sentences.zh: 我不知道，我个人觉得非常感动，我朋友的女儿，一个女大学生，

sentences.en: read this article to me the idea that she's going to go through life feeling like this is not a mystery, that she has some answers, that she knows, you know,
sentences.zh: 把这篇文章读给我听，一想到她将带着这种感觉度过一生——这不再是一个谜，她拥有了一些答案，她知道，你知道，

sentences.en: the range of things that she might expect.
sentences.zh: 她可能会遇到的各种情况。

sentences.en: For me, it always just felt like this wave that was eventually going to come at me and I would just have to kind of figure out how to ride it whenever I got there.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它一直就像是一个迟早会向我袭来的浪潮，而我只需在到达那里时弄清楚如何驾驭它。

sentences.en: You know, whether that was it going to mean I would stop writing, was it going to mean that I felt nothing, as many women do, many women have minimal symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，无论是这意味着我会停止写作，还是意味着我会毫无感觉，就像许多女性一样，许多女性的症状很轻微。

sentences.en: It's my hope that the information is out there and that women going through it don't just feel more empowered, but like, you know, all women who are going to get there eventually.
sentences.zh: 我希望这些信息能够传播出去，不仅让正在经历更年期的女性感到更有力量，而且，你知道，让所有终将走到这一阶段的女性也一样。

sentences.en: Well, this woman has definitely been thinking about it in this conversation.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这位女性在这次谈话中绝对一直在思考这个问题。

sentences.en: And yeah, I do feel more confident and more informed to face what will happen to me.
sentences.zh: 而且是的，我确实感到更有信心、更有见识去面对将要发生在我身上的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think what's exciting about this moment, and I do think that, you know, as the media says, like, menopause is having a moment.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这个时刻令人兴奋的地方在于，而且我的确认为，正如媒体所说，更年期正在迎来它的高光时刻。

sentences.en: I don't think it's really just about menopause and I don't think it's just about the symptoms and I don't think it's just about the treatment,
sentences.zh: 我不认为这仅仅关乎更年期，我也不认为这仅仅关乎症状，我更不认为这仅仅关乎治疗，

sentences.en: although all of that is really important.
sentences.zh: 尽管所有这些都非常重要。

sentences.en: I think it's a moment of women who are older saying, we are important and the things that we care about are important and the things that we are talking about among ourselves,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个年长女性发声的时刻：我们很重要，我们所关心的事情很重要，我们在彼此之间谈论的事情，

sentences.en: that's important not just to us, or at least it should be important to people other than us.
sentences.zh: 这些不仅对我们重要，或者至少它应该对我们之外的人也很重要。

sentences.en: And maybe that important moment that you're describing that older women saying that we matter will feed back into the doctor's office and will feed back into those appointments where women go to find solutions and discuss menopause and their symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 也许你所描述的那个重要时刻——年长女性宣称我们很重要——将会反馈到医生的诊室里，反馈到女性寻求解决方案、讨论更年期及症状的那些预约中。

sentences.en: And their care in general.
sentences.zh: 以及她们的整体医疗护理。

sentences.en: Yeah, I like to think that there could be a kind of virtuous cycle in which, you know, older women feel that they are being heard in the doctor's office, which is, of course,
sentences.zh: 是的，我愿意相信可能会有一种良性循环，你知道，年长女性觉得她们在诊所里得到了倾听，这当然，

sentences.en: not divorced from culture itself.
sentences.zh: 与文化本身并非毫无关系。

sentences.en: They do interact and that their care in general might even improve.
sentences.zh: 它们确实相互影响，她们的整体医疗护理甚至可能会有所改善。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like maybe they won't be just offhand rebuffed.
sentences.zh: 也许她们不会再随随便便地被回绝了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like you were.
sentences.zh: 就像你当年的遭遇一样。

sentences.en: That would be a good outcome for sure.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是一个好的结果。

sentences.en: You know, I want to be clear, like I'm really not here to advocate for menopausal hormone therapy for women because every woman's health condition is different.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想澄清一下，我真的不是来倡导女性使用更年期激素疗法的，因为每个女性的健康状况都不同。

sentences.en: Everybody's risk benefit analysis is different.
sentences.zh: 每个人的风险收益分析都不同。

sentences.en: Everybody's profile is different.
sentences.zh: 每个人的身体状况都不同。

sentences.en: But every woman should have the right to feel that there is time and space for the conversation and to have their symptoms taken seriously, whatever they decide to do.
sentences.zh: 但每个女性都应该有权感觉到有时间和空间来进行这种对话，并且无论她们决定怎么做，她们的症状都能被认真对待。

sentences.en: Susan, thank you.
sentences.zh: 苏珊，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Oh, thanks so much for having me on.
sentences.zh: 哦，非常感谢邀请我参加。

sentences.en: So I'm curious, what did you end up doing?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，你最终是怎么做的？

sentences.en: What did you decide for yourself?
sentences.zh: 你为自己做了什么决定？

sentences.en: I am on, I'm taking estrogen and progesterone, pretty low dose.
sentences.zh: 我在服用，我在服用雌激素和孕激素，剂量相当低。

sentences.en: And I have to say that my hot flashes have completely gone away.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我的潮热已经完全消失了。

sentences.en: And I think I hadn't really appreciated how much they were bothering me until they did go away.
sentences.zh: 而且我不得不承认，在它们消失之前，我并没有真正意识到它们对我的困扰有多大。

sentences.en: But I probably won't stay on them for more than five years at most because I do have a slightly elevated risk of breast cancer given my family history.
sentences.zh: 但我大概不会连续服用超过五年，最多如此，因为考虑到我的家族病史，我患乳腺癌的风险略有升高。

sentences.en: But I know that in five years, I will probably have to do some real thinking and having some conversations and gather information and, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我知道五年后，我可能不得不进行一些真正的思考，进行一些对话，收集信息，并且，你知道，

sentences.en: make the best choice that I think I can make.
sentences.zh: 做出我认为自己能做出的最佳选择。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.zh: 我编写了游戏“连线”（Connections），这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基。

sentences.zh: 我每天负责创作“拼写蜜蜂”（Spelling Bee）和“字母箱”（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉症的东西。

sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.zh: 周四，联邦检察官在针对前总统特朗普卸任后不当处理机密文件的起诉书中增加了重大指控，

sentences.en: saying he told a maintenance worker at Mar-a-Lago to delete potentially incriminating footage from a security camera.
sentences.zh: 称他曾指示海湖庄园的一名维修工删除监控摄像头中可能具有 incriminating（自证其罪）的录像。

sentences.zh: 这些指控似乎增强了检察官在机密文件案中对特朗普的指控力度，

sentences.en: as they prepare to charge him in a second case over his effort to overturn the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 因为他们正准备就他试图推翻 2020 年大选的行动对他提起第二起诉讼。

sentences.en: That indictment is expected to come in the next few days.
sentences.zh: 预计该起起诉书将在未来几天内下达。

sentences.zh: 而且，作为全球变暖的最新证据，据气候专家称，七月份现在有望成为有记录以来最热的一个月。

sentences.en: Last month was the world's hottest June.
sentences.zh: 上个月是世界上最热的六月。

sentences.zh: 到目前为止，2023 年很可能成为世界上最热的一年，取代 2016 年。

sentences.zh: 我们周一见。

sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运转。

sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。
